clue.text: Masefield had butter with salt-cake on this

definitions.text: Masefield had butter with salt-cake on this

parts.words: Masefield had butter with salt-cake on this
parts.note: recalls John Masefield's poem Cargoes, whose dirty British coaster goes butting through the Channel with a salt-caked chimney; the coaster is the butter

explanation.surface: A puzzling note that the poet Masefield ate butter and salt-cake together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the spread but something that butts: the coaster in Masefield's poem Cargoes, which has a salt-caked smoke stack. Salt-cake is also an industrial chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's line describes the ship's funnel, a tall chimney carrying away engine fumes.

clue.text: Series of animal impressions

parts.note: impressions are read as marks pressed into the ground, not a mimic's act

explanation.surface: A run of impersonations of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoor is the track or trail left by a wild beast.

clue.text: Frank gets dismissed, but not in writing

parts.note: a dismissed batsman in cricket is out
something spoken is oral rather than written

explanation.surface: A man called Frank is let go, though not by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspoken means candid and blunt in speech.

clue.text: A call is given me -could be the gospel truth

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A summons has come to me, which might be absolute fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelicalism is Protestant belief centred on the Bible's gospel message.

clue.text: It may be long or short ending to a foot

definitions.text: It may be long or short ending to a foot

parts.words: It may be long or short ending to a foot
parts.note: a foot's end is read literally as what grows at the tip of a toe, kept long or clipped short

explanation.surface: Something long or short that finishes off a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'foot' in poetry has long and short syllables, but here it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny plate covering the tip of each toe, trimmed or left to grow.

clue.text: Indian or Chinese dog .catches stray cat

indicators.note: catches means the dog word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: the chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: stray means the letters of cat wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A Native American or a Chinese dog grabs a wandering cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stray' rearranges CAT into OCTA, which CHOW 'catches' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are a Native American people, called Indians in older usage.

clue.text: Bird without the knowledge to be stylish

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the following letters from the bird's name

parts.note: a chicken is a farmyard bird
ken is one's range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: A bird that lacks the know-how to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue repeats 'stylish be'; the page reads 'to be stylish', with 'to be' as link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a borrowing from French for elegant and fashionable.

clue.text: His excursions go without a hitch

definitions.text: His excursions go without a hitch

parts.words: His excursions go without a hitch
parts.note: without a hitch is read literally: walking trips with no hitching of lifts

explanation.surface: His outings always go smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler who travels on foot rather than thumbing rides.

clue.text: Caretaker, or kind of cicerone, carrying a note in Paris

indicators.note: carrying means the reworked letters hold the note inside
kind of signals a version of the word cicerone with its letters reordered

parts.note: G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A caretaker or tour guide brings a message in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind of' reworks CICERONE into CONCIERE, and 'carrying' puts G inside. 'in Paris' marks the word as French; a cicerone is a guide to sights.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a concierge is the porter or custodian of a block of flats.

clue.text: Under-the-counter merchant may boycott EEC man

parts.note: to black goods is for unions to boycott them
a Marketeer was a supporter of Britain joining the EEC, the Common Market

explanation.surface: An illicit trader might shun a European official.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1970s Britain 'Marketeers' were campaigners for membership of the European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: A black marketeer trades illegally in scarce or controlled goods, sold secretly.

clue.text: Storm follows dismissal for gross offence

indicators.note: follows places the storm word after the dismissal word

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: A tempest comes after someone is sacked for serious misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shocking, scandalous act, an affront.

clue.text: The family is after bribes — a form of protection

indicators.note: is after places the family word behind the bribes word

parts.note: to oil someone's palm is to bribe them, so oils means bribes
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A family pursuing bribes, as a kind of protection racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskin is waterproof cloth or clothing that shields the wearer from rain.

clue.text: Old fighter made tanner a round, say — disgusting!

indicators.note: a round, said aloud, is around, telling us the reworked letters go around the fighter
made, as in made into something new, signals the letters of tanner are rearranged

parts.note: pug is an old short form of pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A veteran boxer forced a leather-worker into a round, which was repellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' reworks TANNER into RENANT; 'a round, say' (sounding like 'around') puts it about PUG. A tanner was also an old British sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant means repellent, causing strong distaste.

clue.text: This may go for a walk about; or soldier on

definitions.text: This may go for a walk

parts.note: c, for circa, is the Latin abbreviation for about
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone may wander about or else carry on doggedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a small dog breed, and dogs are taken out on walks.

clue.text: Countryman gets pasture back with implicit approval

indicators.note: implicit, folded inside, signals that the approval sits within the other piece
back means the pasture word is read from right to left

parts.note: a ley is land temporarily under grass, a meadow
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A rural man retreats to his meadow with tacit permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEY into YEL, and 'implicit' puts OK inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated rustic, a country bumpkin.

clue.text: Boringly spoken wisecrack about the undercover Left

indicators.note: crack means the two letters are split apart to take something in
about means the split letters go around the rest
spoken means wise is heard as the letter name said twice

parts.note: wise sounds like Y's, two of the letter Y
an awning is a canopy one stands under for cover

explanation.surface: A dull, voiced quip about the hidden left-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' hears 'wise' as Y's, two Ys; 'crack' and 'about' split them round AWNING and L. 'wisecrack' wants to be a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a way that makes one gape with boredom, tediously.

clue.text: Mechanism for controlling the seedings at Wimbledon

definitions.text: Mechanism for controlling the seedings at Wimbledon

parts.words: Mechanism for controlling the seedings at Wimbledon
parts.note: seedings are read not as tournament rankings but as grass grown from seed on the courts, kept short by a machine

explanation.surface: A system for managing the tennis rankings at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon's championships are played on grass courts, so 'seedings' points both to ranked players and to grass grown from seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine with blades that cuts grass, keeping a turf court trim.

clue.text: Solution to produce a love match

explanation.surface: The answer is to arrange a romantic pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitewash is a lime solution for painting walls, and in sport a contest where the loser scores nothing.

clue.text: Arthur Pinero's centre Seat for repose

definitions.text: Arthur Pinero's centre Seat for repose

parts.note: the playwright's full name was Arthur Wing Pinero, so his middle name is Wing
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: The comfortable seat at the heart of a playwright's resting place.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Arthur Wing Pinero was a Victorian playwright; 'centre' means his middle name. The whole clue also describes a high-backed armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing chair is an armchair with side projections at head height, made for resting.

clue.text: A looser arrangement of spray-gun

indicators.note: arrangement of signals the letters of a looser are reordered

explanation.surface: A slacker way to set up a paint sprayer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that sprays its contents.

clue.text: Childish kind of hobby

parts.note: hobby is read as a hobby horse, a child's toy steed, rather than a pastime

explanation.surface: An infantile pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocking horse is a toy steed a child sways back and forth on.

clue.text: Increase level of sound

indicators.note: of sound means we want a word heard like a word for level

parts.note: to raze a building is to level it to the ground

explanation.surface: Turn up the volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'level of sound' reads as volume, but 'level' is a verb (raze) and 'of sound' says the answer sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift or increase it.

clue.text: Urge to drive

explanation.surface: An impulse to get behind the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is both to urge someone on and to drive or propel something forward.

clue.text: Sort of code that can deal with long sentences

definitions.text: that can deal with long sentences

explanation.surface: A code that handles lengthy sentences, as a grammar checker might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long sentences' looks grammatical but means prison terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A penal code lists crimes and punishments, and penal means relating to punishment such as jail terms.

clue.text: He plays crooked bat at all times

parts.note: a racket is a bat for tennis or squash
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A cricketer who always uses a bent bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest business, a swindler who cheats.

clue.text: Let some lawyer elicit what's left

indicators.note: some means only part of the words lawyer elicit is used

explanation.surface: Allow a lawyer to draw out the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, a remnant.

clue.text: Old readers begin here

parts.note: readers of the Old Testament start with its first book

explanation.surface: Elderly readers start at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old readers' suggests elderly people, but it means readers of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening book of the Bible, telling of the world's creation.

clue.text: Part of glacier face crumbling in hostile environment

indicators.note: environment, a surrounding, signals that the hostile word encloses the reworked letters

parts.note: ill as in ill will means hostile

indicators.note: crumbling means the letters of face break up and reform

explanation.surface: A section of glacier face collapses in a dangerous setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' turns FACE into CEFA, which ILL surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An icefall is a steep, broken stretch of a glacier, like a frozen waterfall.

clue.text: Food the autocrat at the breakfast table likes the sound of

indicators.note: the sound of says the answer is heard like the thing the autocrat likes

parts.words: the autocrat at the breakfast table likes
parts.note: an autocrat loves to put a yoke on his subjects; also a nod to Oliver Wendell Holmes's book The Autocrat of the Breakfast-Table

explanation.surface: A breakfast-table despot favours the sound of a particular dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue joins 'Food the'. A yoke is a harness and a symbol of subjugation.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow centre of an egg, eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Kind of rule involving a rich logic

indicators.note: involving, in the sense of entangling, signals the letters of a rich logic are mixed up

explanation.surface: A form of government that depends on wealthy reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchic describes government by a small, often wealthy, elite.
